{"id": 164, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — TLG-EM-0414 email thread: Kessler to Okafor, Complex 4 load-shed directive (2025-03-14)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "PRODUCED FROM CUSTODIAN MAILBOX: d.kessler@talvernlogistics.example — Bates TLG-EM-0414 through TLG-EM-0416
CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877

---- Message 3 of 3 ----
From: Dana Kessler, VP Operations, Talvern Logistics Group LLC
To: Ruth Okafor, Site Manager, Silo Complex 4 (Halden Junction)
Cc: Priya Natarajan, Regional Energy Desk
Date: Friday, March 14, 2025, 4:47 PM CT
Subject: RE: RE: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Ruth — decision is made. Effective tonight, take dehumidification units DH-4A, DH-4B, DH-4C and DH-4D at Complex 4 offline on the load-shed schedule, 22:00 to 06:00, and if the demand-charge numbers hold, keep them dark through the shoulder season. Priya's model says Complex 4 climate control is 61 percent of the site's demand charge and we are not clawing back the Q1 overrun any other way.

I am aware of what the Meridian contract says. Section 6.2 of the Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement calls for continuous dehumidification and a ceiling of 55 percent relative humidity in the storage galleries. If Meridian asks, this is routine maintenance on the air-handling side. Log it that way in the site diary. I will take the heat if Meridian notices.

Do not route this through the maintenance ticketing queue — handle it as a local operating instruction from this office.

— DK

---- Message 2 of 3 ----
From: Ruth Okafor
To: Dana Kessler
Date: Friday, March 14, 2025, 3:58 PM CT
Subject: RE: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Dana — before I touch those units I want it in writing. The galleries are holding 1.04 million bushels of Meridian hard red spring wheat right now and the loggers have us at 52 to 54 percent RH with all four units running. If we shed them overnight in March we will drift over spec within days. Please confirm you are directing the power-down notwithstanding the WCSA humidity clause.

---- Message 1 of 3 ----
From: Priya Natarajan, Regional Energy Desk
To: Dana Kessler
Date: Thursday, March 13, 2025, 11:12 AM CT
Subject: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Dana — attached is the demand-charge workup. Complex 4 is the outlier in the region. The only lever big enough this quarter is the dehumidification bank. Flagging for your call; this desk does not have authority over leased-site climate equipment."}

{"id": 165, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — TLG-EM-0419 email: Okafor implementation confirmation, Complex 4 power-down (2025-03-15)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "PRODUCED FROM CUSTODIAN MAILBOX: r.okafor@talvernlogistics.example — Bates TLG-EM-0419
CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877

From: Ruth Okafor, Site Manager, Silo Complex 4 (Halden Junction)
To: Dana Kessler, VP Operations
Cc: Night Shift Distribution — Complex 4
Date: Saturday, March 15, 2025, 7:21 AM CT
Subject: Complex 4 — load-shed executed per your 3/14 instruction

Dana —

Confirming execution of your written instruction of yesterday afternoon. Units DH-4A through DH-4D were de-energized at 23:10 last night by the night crew. Per your direction the action is entered in the site diary as 'routine maintenance — air handling, scheduled,' and no ticket was opened in the maintenance queue.

Two operational notes for the record:

1. Alarm handling. The gallery humidity sensors are hard-wired to the annunciator panel and would have chimed continuously overnight. I authorized the shift lead to mute the RH set-point alarms for the duration of the load-shed window so the panel is not screaming at the crew. The mute is logged on the panel itself.

2. Drift. As of the 06:30 walk-through this morning the north gallery loggers read 58 percent RH and the south gallery 63 percent RH, against the 55 percent ceiling in the Meridian agreement. That is one night. If the units stay dark on the schedule you described — and certainly if they stay dark through the shoulder season — the galleries will run well over spec and the wheat will take on moisture. I have said my piece on this and will follow the instruction as given.

Re-energization will occur only on written direction from your office, per your note. The crew has standing instructions not to restart the bank on their own initiative.

Ruth Okafor
Site Manager, Complex 4 — Halden Junction
Talvern Logistics Group LLC"}
